title: Canonical diagonal affine trace source coordinates
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient data of [def-pur-conventions], a positive coefficient level, and its datum $P$ in the indexing of [def-pur-affine-diagonal-tate-coordinates]. Write $A=P.\mathrm{Coefficient}$ for the recorded lifted finite quotient and use the tensor, pullback and shifted diagonal Tate coefficient of [def-pur-smooth-purity-map], the compact-support realization of [def-pur-smooth-trace], and the actual site comparisons and ordered coordinate counits of [def-pur-proetale-ordered-integration]. Let $S$ be Noetherian with $\ell$ invertible, $d\geq0$, and $r\geq1$ with $\ell^rA=0$. Put $N=\ell^r$, $p:V=\mathbf A^d_S\to S$ in the ordered affine-line tower, $L_r(T)=(\mu_{N,T}^{\mathrm{et}}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/N}A_T)^{\otimes_A d}[2d]$, and $J_{K_0}=Lp^*K_0\otimes_A^L L_r(V)$. All exponents and positive coefficient levels are retained.

Define OrdinarySource to be $J_{K_0}$, TateSupport to be $Rp_!^pC_VL_r(V)$, and IntegrationSupport to be $Rp_!^pC_VJ_{K_0}$. Define coefficientIso by ordered-right-tower coefficient descent followed by the base-coefficient pullback identification. Define ordinarySourceIso from $Rp_!^eL_r(V)$ to the ordered left tower applied to the ordered right tower on the unit by compact-support image of coefficientIso inverse and inverse ordered compact-support comparison. Define ordinaryTrace by ordinarySourceIso followed by the actual ordered restrictions of the normalized projective-line counits. Define ordinaryIntegration by the inverse coefficient-first projection, tensor with ordinaryTrace and the right unitor, with the Koszul source symmetries of [def-pur-tensor-trace-projection-arrows]; ordinaryTranspose is its specified ordinary exceptional adjoint transpose.

Define counitSource by the actual proper/open compact-support site comparison followed by $C_S$ of ordinarySourceIso. Define proTrace by counitSource followed by the independently constructed ordered pro-etale coordinate counit. For $K_0$ bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude as in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], projectionIso is the unique isomorphism
$$Rp_!^pC_VJ_{K_0}\ \simeq\ C_SK_0\otimes_A^L Rp_!^pC_VL_r(V)$$
whose inverse is the recorded coefficient-first projection with its tensor/pullback source comparison. ProjectionIsoType and ProjectionIsoSpec name this isomorphism type and this inverse-map condition. Define proIntegration by projectionIso, tensor with proTrace and the right unitor. The unique isomorphism exists on this stated finite-Tor domain. Define exponentIso from $L_r$ to $P$'s diagonal-exponent coefficient by the normalized root-power transition or its inverse, according to the order of the exponents.

More generally, sourceCoordinates is the following canonical source isomorphism: given a fixed-scalar pro-etale complex $K$, an ordinary $K_0$, a representing isomorphism $C_SK_0\simeq K$, and an ordinary coefficient $L\simeq P.\mathrm{diagonalTwistEtale}(V,d)$, compose the recorded twist-and-shift reassociation of the purity source, the pullback comparison at that representing isomorphism, the image of the inverse coefficient isomorphism, and inverse tensor comparison. Its target is $C_V(Lp^*K_0\otimes_A^L L)$.

For the intrinsic realization coordinates, suppose additionally that $a_S:S\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite type, let $K$ be an intrinsic pro-etale module complex, and let $C_SK_0\simeq E_S^{-1}K$ be a representing isomorphism for the recorded realization equivalence $E_S$. MapPair is the type of pairs of morphisms $(M\to M',\ Rp_!^pM''\to K)$ in intrinsic coordinates, retaining their computed endpoints; SameMaps compares both morphisms by heterogeneous equality. Given the coefficient source identification above and an integration arrow $Rp_!^pC_VJ_{K_0}\to C_SK_0$, transportCoordinates constructs this pair by applying sourceCoordinates and $C_V$(ordinaryTranspose), the exceptional comparison given by the image of the comparison unit, and the representing isomorphism for the first component. For the second it applies compact support of sourceCoordinates, the intrinsic support realization comparison, the supplied integration arrow, the representing isomorphism, and the realization counit. Thus these comparison maps are fixed independently of any purity map. IntegrationInput is the corresponding integration Hom type expressed using $P$'s coefficient alias. IntegrationSiteSquare abbreviates the actual proper/open compact-support comparison equation between proIntegration and $C_S$(ordinaryIntegration) on $J_{K_0}$. ProjectiveNormalization abbreviates $t_q^ph_q^p=1$ on the prescribed infinity Kummer class.

For these constructions, the affine tower projection is smooth of relative dimension $d$ (over every scheme); the shifted root coefficient is bounded below whenever $N$ is positive and invertible on its scheme; and every positive power of an invertible prime is invertible. No divisibility of the coefficient level by a ramification index, and no flatness over $\mathbf Z/\ell^r$, is imposed.

The constituent definitions are owned by [def-pur-proetale-ordered-integration], [def-pur-finite-site-tensor-projection], [def-pur-finite-site-coordinates], [def-sf-compact-support-site-comparison-construction], [def-pur-bounded-site-transpose-arrows], [def-pur-supported-projective-chern], [def-pur-supported-projective-site-arrows], [def-pur-proetale-affine-line-counit], [def-amb-affine-trace-tower], [def-amb-affine-linear-trace-action], [def-amb-vector-integration-charts], [def-pur-tensor-trace-projection-arrows]. These supply the ordered pro-etale counit, coefficient-first projection and tensor comparison, finite Tate exponent transitions, proper/open support comparison, exceptional comparison unit, projective Kummer class and trace, infinity Cartier datum, affine coordinate tower, ordinary ordered coefficient and compact-support comparisons, and coefficient pullback on vector-bundle charts, respectively. The ordinary ordered left/right functors and counit used in ordinarySourceIso and ordinaryTrace are those of [def-amb-affine-trace-construction].

source.place: Kummer normalization sentence: coefficient, shift, projection and site source coordinates for the affine model.

proof.text: Auxiliary projectionSmooth: induct on the ordered affine-line tower. At zero the projection is the identity, smooth of relative dimension zero. The next coordinate projection is smooth of relative dimension one by AffineSpace.smoothOfRelativeDimension_over. Compose with the induction hypothesis using Mathlib smoothOfRelativeDimension_comp and commute 1+d to d+1. This works over every scheme.

Auxiliary coefficientPlus: signed Tate multiplication at degrees 1 and -1 gives a tensor inverse to the degree-one finite Tate line, so ObjectProperty.flat_of_tensorIso proves its flatness without finiteness of A. Its degree-zero single object has Tor amplitude [0,0]. Induct on the recursive ordered tensor coefficient, starting with the ordinary unit in degree zero. Tensoring the previous bounded-below object with this flat single object preserves its lower bound by DerivedCategory.isGE_tensor_of_torAmplitudeIn. The canonical tensor-shift isomorphism and braiding identify the successor coefficient with that tensor shifted by 2. The t-structure shift rule lowers the bound by 2. This includes d=0, zero coefficients, N=1, and the empty base.
Auxiliary powerUnit: rewrite the natural-number cast of the prime power as the power of its cast using Nat.cast_pow, and apply IsUnit.pow to the supplied base unit.

For the proper part g of the chosen affine-projection compactification, quasi-compactness of the Noetherian base and finite type give a uniform natural bound d on all fibre dimensions. Every finite-A module sheaf is torsion as an abelian sheaf. The proper torsion direct-image theorem gives vanishing above 2d; the canonical module/abelian comparison and faithful forgetting yield the same bound for module higher direct images.

Apply the finite-cohomological-dimension unbounded comparison theorem to the actual adjunction mate at i_!W and at i_!W tensor Lg*K. The finite étale proper projection formula is invertible for arbitrary complexes. Compatibility of comparison with the pullback tensor comparisons transports its projection map to the pro-etale map. Extension by zero commutes with comparison, and the remaining compactification projection factors are isomorphisms.

Unfold the coefficient-first projection: tensor symmetries, the compactification projection just proved invertible, and the inverse source comparison are isomorphisms. Take the inverse of asIso of this very morphism. Its inverse is definitionally the required map, so ProjectionIsoSpec holds. For any other candidate its inverse condition gives equality of inverses; Iso.inv_eq_inv and Iso.ext give equality of isomorphisms. The argument needs neither invertibility of the coefficient exponent on S nor finite Tor amplitude of K, so it proves the existing signature verbatim.

proof_origin.place: Inverse coefficient-first projection in the affine-model normalization. Extend the canonical comparison mate by finite étale cohomological dimension (Stacks 095U, 0A3V and 07K7) and transport the existing finite projection formula; no statement or definition changes.
